NEW PATIENT VISIT

54-year-old man establishing care. Long-haul truck driver, usually out 10-12 days at a stretch, home 3-4 days. Married, lives in Chicopee. Came fasting.

Brings: type 2 diabetes since 2004 (diagnosed at about age 40), high blood pressure and high cholesterol, both treated for about as long as the diabetes. Follows with an outside endocrinology group for the diabetes and an outside cardiology group for blood pressure; plans to keep both. Wants us as home base, labs here when possible since our draw station opens early.

Current medications (bottles reviewed, all filled within the last 2 months):
- metformin 1000 mg twice daily with meals
- lisinopril 20 mg daily
- amlodipine 5 mg daily
- hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg every morning
- atorvastatin 40 mg daily
Says he rarely misses a dose; keeps the pill organizer in the cab. Some days the evening metformin slips when he eats late.

Allergies: NKDA.
Surgical history: none.
Family history: father with type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure and sleep apnea. Mother with high blood pressure and high cholesterol. Paternal uncle with coronary artery disease.
Social: former smoker, about 20 pack-years, quit 03/2011. Alcohol 1-2 drinks a month. No other substances. Eats most meals at truck stops; tries to pick the grilled options "when they have them." No regular exercise.

ROS: no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no foot numbness or sores, no vision change, no urinary symptoms. Otherwise negative as asked.

Exam
BP 147/94, HR 69, RR 12, T 36.4, SpO2 97% RA. Wt 101.5 kg, Ht 178.2 cm, BMI 32.0.
Well appearing, pleasant. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart: regular rate and rhythm, S1 S2 normal, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender, central adiposity. Extremities without edema.
Feet: skin intact, no calluses or ulcers, DP and PT pulses 2+ bilaterally, 10 g monofilament felt at all sites tested both feet.
PHQ-2: 0.

Assessment / Plan
1. Type 2 diabetes, on metformin. A1c, BMP, CBC, urine albumin/creatinine today. Foot exam normal. Asked him to send us his last outside eye exam if he has one.
2. Essential hypertension on lisinopril, amlodipine and HCTZ. 147/94 today, above goal. First visit, rushed in from the parking lot; nurse BP recheck in about 4 weeks before deciding anything. He has a home cuff, will log a few morning readings.
3. Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 40. Lipid panel today.
4. Obesity, BMI 32. Talked about truck-stop food choices and walking laps at fuel stops. He is skeptical but willing.
5. Former smoker, quit 2011, 20 pack-years. Not yet in a lung screening group by current criteria; revisit as guidelines change.
6. Health maintenance: flu shot today. One-time hepatitis C and HIV screening ordered, he agreed. Prior records requested for colonoscopy and immunization history. Shingles vaccine to discuss next visit.

Return: nurse BP check ~4 weeks; diabetes follow-up in January.

documents.title: Upper endoscopy (EGD) with biopsy
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
UPPER ENDOSCOPY (EGD) — PROCEDURE NOTE
Date: 08/02/2023
Indication: dysphagia to solids and liquids, regurgitation.
Consent: risks, benefits and alternatives discussed; written consent obtained.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. Tolerated well, no complications.
Findings:
- Esophagus: dilated lumen with retained food residue. The lower esophageal sphincter is tight and does not relax with swallowing; the scope passed into the stomach with gentle pressure. Mucosa without mass. Biopsies taken from the esophagus.
- Stomach: normal.
- Duodenum: normal to the second portion.
Impression: dilated esophagus with retained food and a non-relaxing lower esophageal sphincter. Biopsies pending.
Estimated blood loss: minimal.

events.reason: Esophageal biopsy pathology and GI follow-up letter

reports.text:
SURGICAL PATHOLOGY
Specimen: esophagus, biopsies (multiple fragments).
Gross: several tan soft-tissue fragments, submitted entirely.
Microscopic: squamous mucosa with preserved maturation. No dysplasia or malignancy. No increase in intraepithelial eosinophils. No fungal organisms identified.
reports.conclusion: Esophageal biopsies: benign squamous mucosa. Negative for malignancy. No eosinophilic infiltration.

documents.title: Gastroenterology letter: biopsy results
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY — RESULTS LETTER
Date: 08/08/2023
Re: Lamar Bryant (DOB 02/26/1964)
To: primary care

The esophageal biopsies from Mr. Bryant's endoscopy on 08/02/2023 have returned. They show no malignancy and no eosinophilic infiltration.

Taken together with his six months of progressive dysphagia to solids and liquids, regurgitation of undigested food, and the endoscopic findings of a dilated esophagus holding food residue with a lower esophageal sphincter that fails to relax, the diagnosis is achalasia.

I have discussed these results with Mr. Bryant by telephone.
